NAME: Three-Year Clean Working-Capital Margin
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(NEG(ABS(RATIO(SUB(SUB(DELTA(act, 1), DELTA(che, 1)), SUB(DELTA(lct, 1), DELTA(dlc, 1))), at)))), RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3), VOL(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Low noncash working-capital accruals combined with strong, stable three-period gross margins should predict higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This isolates the persistence-horizon design choice in the strongest prior mechanism: credible margins that do not require working-capital accumulation. The shorter quality window should improve coverage and react more quickly to deterioration while retaining enough history to distinguish durable margins from one-period profitability.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Retained Earnings Clean-Build Bottleneck
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 5)), RANK(NEG(MA(ABS(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), at)), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should earn higher returns when retained earnings accumulate persistently without recurring working-capital accrual investment.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The minimum approximates a conjunctive double sort, requiring both retained earnings growth and clean working-capital conversion. It repairs the unstable small-denominator ratio used previously, which produced a positive cross-sectional slope but a negative long-short alpha, while preserving the underlying internal-capital-formation mechanism.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Accounting-Slack Solvency Bottleneck
EXPRESSION: RANK(NEG(MAX(RANK(MA(RATIO(ADD(ABS(txach), ABS(aoloch)), at), 3)), RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should earn higher returns only when both opaque accrual activity and debt pressure are low.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The prior joint-high penalty allowed highly levered firms or firms with large opaque accruals into the long side whenever the other dimension was benign, potentially explaining its opposite-signed Fama-MacBeth slope. Using the maximum of the two bad-state ranks imposes a clean-accounting-and-financial-slack bottleneck, producing a more monotonic cross-sectional ordering.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Inventory-Cost Absorption Gap
EXPRESSION: RANK(NEG(WINSOR(SUB(TREND(RATIO(NEG(invch), at), 3), TREND(RATIO(cogs, at), 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms should underperform when inventory investment accelerates persistently faster than the cost throughput supported by current operations.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Negated invch represents inventory investment under the cash-flow-statement sign convention, while cost of goods sold captures realized inventory throughput. The directional trend gap distinguishes potentially excessive inventory accumulation from the previously tested unsigned volatility mechanism and avoids treating demand-supported inventory growth as generic accrual noise.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Margin-to-Working-Capital Trend Spread
EXPRESSION: RANK(WINSOR(SUB(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5), TREND(RATIO(wcap, sale), 5)), 1))
HYPOTHESIS: Margin improvement should predict higher returns when it outpaces the growth of working capital required per unit of sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The signal directly compares the trajectory of operating profitability with the trajectory of capital trapped in working capital. Rising margins accompanied by an equal or larger increase in working-capital intensity are less likely to represent durable cash earnings, whereas improving margins with flat or falling working-capital needs indicate better cash conversion.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Debt-Adjusted Cash Retention
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(re, at), 5)), RANK(SUB(TREND(RATIO(che, at), 5), TREND(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at), 5))))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent retained earnings should predict higher returns when accompanied by cash accumulation that is not financed by increasing debt.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Retained earnings provide the reported-performance channel, while debt-adjusted cash growth tests whether that performance is realized as internally generated liquidity. The conjunctive score improves on an unsupported-retained-earnings gap by requiring positive confirmation from both cumulative earnings and financing-adjusted cash accumulation.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Receivable-Neutral Earnings Durability
EXPRESSION: RANK(SUB(MA(RATIO(ADD(ni, recch), at), 3), VOL(RATIO(ADD(ni, recch), at), 3)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms with high and stable earnings after removing the receivable-accrual contribution should earn higher subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Under the cash-flow-statement convention, recch offsets the receivable component embedded in net income, so ADD(ni, recch) approximates earnings after receivable cash conversion. Measuring the persistence and stability of this adjusted earnings stream replaces the prior window tweak with a direct redefinition of quality based on cash realization.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Opaque Accrual Reversal Load
EXPRESSION: RANK(NEG(WINSOR(RATIO(ABS(TS_SUM(RATIO(aoloch, at), 3)), TS_SUM(ABS(RATIO(ni, at)), 3)), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Persistent same-direction other accrual adjustments relative to the scale of reported earnings should predict lower subsequent returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio
REASONING: Temporary accruals should reverse, so summing signed other-accrual adjustments allows genuine reversals to cancel while persistent accounting flows accumulate. Scaling by cumulative earnings magnitude creates a continuous accounting-noise load without reusing leverage or collapsing the long portfolio into a generic low-leverage sort.

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Supplier-Neutral Cash-Profit Persistence
EXPRESSION: TS_SUM(MUL(INDICATOR(RATIO(ni, at), 0), SIGN(RATIO(SUB(oancf, apalch), at))), 3)
HYPOTHESIS: Repeated reported profits should predict higher returns when operating cash flow remains positive after removing cash support from changes in accounts payable and accrued liabilities.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Each profitable period receives a positive contribution if supplier-financing-adjusted cash flow is positive and a negative contribution if the profit lacks adjusted cash backing. Nonprofitable periods are neutral, so the construction contrasts cash-confirmed and supplier-funded profit persistence without forcing a screened-out group into an extreme portfolio leg.

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Cash-Converted Margin Improvement
EXPRESSION: MIN(RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale), 5)), RANK(NEG(MA(RATIO(DELTA(wcap, 1), sale), 3))))
HYPOTHESIS: Improving gross margins should predict higher returns when they are accompanied by low working-capital investment relative to sales.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
REASONING: Cross-sectional ranks place margin improvement and working-capital accruals on a common scale, eliminating domination by the unbounded working-capital ratio. Using the working-capital change rather than its sign-unstable level focuses the second channel on incremental cash absorption, while the minimum requires both margin improvement and clean cash conversion.
